summary: runtime.kubernetes.session_store (pvc, the default, or postgres) with session_dsn_secret. Under postgres every pod of a tree gets OMP_SESSION_STORAGE=sql and OMP_SESSION_SQL_DSN_FILE=/var/run/legion/providers/<key> from the one podEnvironment seam; the resume path keeps ompSessionFile and --resume under both stores; affinity and the sessions subPath mount are unchanged; the worker-image probe requires session-storage=probed in the probe pod's log under postgres and records sessionStorageProbed in its cache. No smoke rig, scratch daemon, kind cluster, NATS container, or tmux server was started (Sami, 2026-09-13 19:00Z). Proof is the daemon's own suite plus the pull request's CI.

The exact commands the tester records without running are the plan handoff's testPlan["5"] (kind create cluster --name legion-81; a postgres:16 container on the kind network; the kind overlay with SESSION_DSN in providers.env and session_store: postgres / session_dsn_secret: SESSION_DSN in legion.yaml; kubectl apply -k; the daemon log line 'probe pod … passed: probe-image: OK … session-storage=probed'; an admitted issue's architect pod showing both OMP_SESSION_* variables via kubectl exec env; one omp_session_files row; delete the pod and see 'resurrecting <KEY> by resuming OMP session <path>' with generation g2 carrying --resume=<path>; the negative control of removing SESSION_DSN from the Secret → a Failed pod quoting 'OMP_SESSION_SQL_DSN_FILE names /var/run/legion/providers/SESSION_DSN, which could not be read'; teardown).
trickyParts: config.ts cannot value-import boot-probes.ts: boot-probes.ts:57 computes IMAGE_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS from config.ts's DEFAULT_SLOW_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS at module top level, so the cycle config → boot-probes → config throws a TDZ ReferenceError whenever config.ts loads first (proved with a two-file Bun repro before deciding). Both Oh My Pi variable names therefore live in k8s-manifests.ts (a runtime leaf: only type imports from config/k8s-client) and boot-probes.ts imports SESSION_STORAGE_VARIABLE from there — one definition on main, no cycle.

The init container's LEGION_RESUME_SESSION_FILE stat would fail every postgres resume (the transcript is a database row, not a file in the volume's sessions/ directory): the runtime now passes resumeSessionFile to buildPodManifest only under pvc, while --resume still reaches OMP under both stores. Read at the pinned fork tag v18.1.21-sami.20260914-080519, packages/coding-agent/src/session/session-manager.ts #setSessionFile: an explicit --resume path with no entries 'start[s] fresh but keep[s] the requested path' — so under postgres the same-agent invariant has no stat-equivalent without a database query, which nothing in the pod path makes today. Reported to the architect.

The OK line's suffix order on main is `probe-image: OK (<omp>) session-storage=probed daemon-api-version=<N>` (cmdProbeImage); the marker check is `includes`, never a full-line match, and the daemon-api-version regex (`daemon-api-version=(\d+)$`) is unaffected because the marker precedes it.

buildPodManifest appends LEGION_TERMINATION_GRACE_SECONDS to the main env, so the 'nothing else changes' proof compares the postgres pod's env against a pvc pod's env from a second harness rather than against the POD_ENV fixture.
deviations: Architect brief item 2 said SESSION_STORAGE_VARIABLE is exported from boot-probes.ts on main: it is not (a bare `const` at boot-probes.ts:394); and importing it into config.ts from boot-probes.ts would be the module cycle above. Both names are defined once in k8s-manifests.ts beside PROVIDERS_DIR (the plan's own task-3 placement) and boot-probes.ts imports the first; no second copy exists on main.

Under session_store: postgres the runtime does not hand the init container LEGION_RESUME_SESSION_FILE (see trickyParts). The plan's 'init container untouched / init env unchanged under postgres' assumption would have pinned a broken resume; the spec's acceptance 3 ('resurrection uses it under both stores') needs this for a real postgres pod to start at all. This is the one behaviour beyond 'the two variables' and it is a correctness fix, not scope growth.

The three commits are grouped as config+runtime (acceptance 1–4), probe (acceptance 7), docs — instead of the plan's four — so every commit typechecks on its own: KubernetesRuntimeConfig.sessionStore is a required field, and its test fixtures (runtime-kubernetes.test.ts, runtime.contract.test.ts, index.test.ts) must change in the same commit that adds it.
